newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: More soldiers arrested in Burkina Faso crackdown.
newsitem.headline: More soldiers arrested in Burkina Faso crackdown.

text.p: Burkina Faso has widened a crackdown on elements of the presidential guard accused of gross indiscipline, an official daily said on Thursday.

Sidwaya, which on Tuesday broke the news of the arrest of 17 soldiers, also reported that the ringleader of the group, Chief Adjutant Hyacinthe Kafando, had taken refuge in the French embassy in Ivory Coast.
French embassy officials denied any knowledge of Kafando, who was on a course in Morocco when his followers were first arrested in a security sweep on Sunday and Monday.
The newspaper said the number of soldiers rounded up since then had risen to 25.

Military sources said the arrests followed a growing feud within units responsible for the security of President Blaise Compaore. The president is preparing to host French President Jacques Chirac and several African leaders at a Franco-African summit in Ougadougou in two months.
Campaore unexpectedly cancelled an official trip to Libya last month, but there has been no sign of extra security around his palace or other strategic points in the capital.
The head of state will next week mark the ninth anniversary of his taking power following a coup on October 15, 1987 in which then president Captain Thomas Sankara was killed.
Members of the presidential security are from the National Commando Training Centre in the southern town of Po, which was once commanded by Compaore.
The newspaper said in its first report those arrested were close to Kafando, who is said to be close to Compaore.
It described him as a "feared officer" who led his men into "acts contrary to military discipline".
"The arrests were of a preventive nature to avert a settling of scores in this specialised unit of the army," it added.
